original_question: Can a 3-dimensional sphere admit two non-proportional projectively equivalent metrics of Lorentzian signature?
target_in_paper: Section 12, Question 12.0.5 in the final arXiv v3 / journal version: the existence of two non-proportional projectively equivalent Lorentzian metrics on S^3. An earlier workshop PDF version phrased the terminal question more broadly with indefinite signature, but the final arXiv/journal formulation is specifically Lorentzian. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to perfect: it names the correct manifold (the 3-dimensional sphere), asks the correct existence question, uses the correct relation ('projectively equivalent'), requires the metrics to be non-proportional, and matches the sharpened final-signature restriction in the paper (Lorentzian). In fact, it is essentially the final official wording of the question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
missing_details: State explicitly that the manifold is the smooth closed manifold S^3, not an arbitrary topological 3-sphere. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

Define 'projectively equivalent' for metrics as: they have the same geodesics when these geodesics are regarded as unparameterized curves. This is the nearby equivalence used in Section 12. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

Define 'non-proportional' as: the two metrics are not related by h = c g for any nonzero constant c; the paper explicitly contrasts this with the trivial fact that g and const·g always have the same geodesics. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
Make the quantifier explicit by asking whether there exist Lorentzian metrics g and h on S^3 with these properties. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))

If maximum stand-alone precision is desired, spell out that on a 3-manifold 'Lorentzian' means signature (2,1) up to sign convention. This is implicit rather than separately restated in the paper. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
refined_question: Does the smooth manifold S^3 admit two Lorentzian metrics g and h, of signature (2,1), that are projectively equivalent in the sense that they have the same geodesics as unparameterized curves, but are not proportional by any nonzero constant factor?
equivalent_formulation: Do there exist Lorentzian metrics g and h on S^3 with the same unparameterized geodesics such that h ≠ c g for every nonzero constant c? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
justification: The draft is targeting the exact question asked at the end of Section 12. In the surrounding discussion, the paper first defines projective equivalence for connections via equation (12.3) and explains that the corresponding metric-level problem is to understand when different metrics have the same geodesics as unparameterized curves. It then says that the broader global problem is to understand the topology of closed manifolds admitting non-proportional projectively equivalent metrics of indefinite signature, and isolates the S^3 Lorentzian case as 'the simplest version' of that problem. Therefore the refined question should stay exactly at the level of existence of two Lorentzian metrics on S^3 with the same unparameterized geodesics and should not be broadened to arbitrary closed manifolds or to arbitrary indefinite signature. Also, your wording is especially faithful because the final arXiv/journal version uses 'Lorentzian signature'; the older workshop PDF had a broader 'indefinite signature' wording. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1308.5417))
